title: Dynamic Changes in Tumor Microenvironment and TP53 Mutation in EGFR-Mutated Lung Cancer Post-TKI Treatment: Implications for Immunotherapy Prediction
description: This project gathers paired sample data from NSCLC patients pre- and post-TKI treatment, aiming to analyze the dynamic evolution of the microenvironment induced by TKI and to explore potential treatment options, such as immunotherapy, after the development of TKI resistance.

title: Bulk RNA-seq of Microenvironmental Prostaglandin F2-alpha Antagonizes Tumoral FSP1 to Unleash Ferroptosis and Immunotherapy vulnerability
description: Bulk RNA-seq was performed on A375 cells treated with sgCtrl or sgFSP1, each with three biological replicates. Total RNA was extracted using Magzol reagent (Magen, R4801). Subsequent library construction and sequencing were conducted by BGI Genomics Co., Ltd., and all raw reads underwent rigorous quality control.

title: Neoadjuvant Sintilimab and Chemotherapy for Resectable Stage IIIA Non-small-cell Lung Cancer
description: Evidence of neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy for locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer remains investigational and requires prospective validation. This phase II trial aimed to investigate the safety and effectiveness of neoadjuvant PD-1 inhibitor sintilimab in addition to chemotherapy in the management of resectable stage IIIA non-small cell lung cancer. Eligible patients received two to four 21-day cycles of neoadjuvant therapy: sintilimab (200 mg) and carboplatin (area under the curve 5) on day 1, gemcitabine (1000 mg/m2) on day 1 and day 8 for squamous cell carcinoma, or pemetrexed (500 mg/m2) on day 1 for adenocarcinoma and non-small cell lung cancer not otherwise specified. The primary endpoints were adverse events and major pathological response. The secondary endpoint was disease-free survival at 1 year. Neoadjuvant sintilimab with platinum-containing dual-agent chemotherapy was feasible and safe for patients with resectable stage IIIA non-small cell lung cancer.

title: Neoadjuvant Camrelizumab Plus Chemotherapy or Apatinib for Resectable and Initially Unresectable Stage II-III Non-small-cell Lung Cancer: A Multicentre, Multi-cohort, Non-randomised, Phase 2 Study
description: This study aimed to explore the efficacy, safety and potential predictive biomarkers of neoadjuvant camrelizumab plus chemotherapy or apatinib in patients with potentially resectable (including initially unresectable) stage II-III NSCLC.

title: Safety, effectiveness and RNA-seq analysis of neoadjuvant PD-1 inhibitor plus chemotherapy in NSCLC
description: This trial aimed to analyze the safety, effectiveness and RNA-seq of neoadjuvant Toripalimab, a humanized PD-1 inhibitor, plus chemotherapy in non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

title: Single nucleus RNA sequencing data from human fetal lung tissue of twin-twin transfusion syndrome
description: We have employed a single cell sequencing approach using 10x Genomics snRNA-seq to study Twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS). TTTS is a rare complication of monochorionic twin pregnancies, caused by abnormal placental vascular anastomoses leading to imbalanced blood flow between the donor and recipient twins. The disturbed hemodynamics clinically manifests as insufficient blood volume in the donor and volume overload in the recipient, which may have profound effects on fetal lung development. In this study, we performed snRNA-seq on lung tissues from TTTS fetuses after termination of pregnancy, providing an unprecedented resolution for analyzing transcriptomic changes associated with the unique hemodynamic environment of TTTS and offering new insights into the molecular mechanisms of lung development under the circulatory disorders caused by TTTS.

title: Circulating tumor DNA has strong prognostic value in extensive-stage small cell lung cancer receiving Toripalimab and Anlotinib maintenance therapy
description: Here, in a phase II clinical trial involving 20 patients with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer who achieved disease control under chemotherapy, we collected plasma samples at three times during toripalimab and anlotinib maintenance therapy and subjected them to ultradeep targeted DNA sequencing, to explore the value of ctDNA.

Samples from tumor, adjacent normal lung tissue, tpMLN, tdMLN, and blood were profiled by scRNA-seq and scTCR/BCR-seq. Postoperative blood was used for bulk TCR/BCR tracking.

description: This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of anlotinib plus penpulimab as a second-line treatment for recurrent extensive-stage small cell lung cancer. The findings may provide a novel therapeutic option for patients with platinum-resistant extensive-stage small cell lung cancer and offer evidence to further optimize precision treatment strategies for this population

title: Co-culturing Lung Cancer Organoids and Lymphocytes Derived from Malignant Serous Effusion Potentially Implements Personalized Immunotherapy
organization: Guangdong Lung Cancer Institute, Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital, Guangdong Academy of Medical Sciences, Guangzhou, 510080, China
description: Specimens were collected from advanced lung cancer patients for organoid culture and a co-culture system. Olink proteomics, flow cytometry analysis and single-cell RNA sequencing indicated the presence of anti-tumor immune activity and supported the functional efficacy of the co-culture system. Chi-square analysis revealed a statistically significant association between the sample type and success of establishment . In samples with matched clinical regimens, receiver operating characteristic analysis based on cell viability reduction identified a diagnostic threshold of >31.93%. Using the co-culture system of LCOs and pleural fluid-derived lymphocytes, the concordance between drug sensitivity and clinical efficacy was 78.6% for immunotherapy and 70.0% for targeted therapy or chemotherapy. Notably, drug sensitivity testing in the established co-culture system demonstrated high concordance with observed clinical efficacy and may be implemented in personalized immunotherapy.

title: Epigenetic Dysregulation Permits E2F1 Activation-Mediated Neuroendocrine Transformation in EGFR-Mutant Lung Adenocarcinoma
organization: Nanjing Medical University Affiliated Cancer Hospital

title: Upregulation of Trop2 in Drug-Tolerant Persister Cells: A Therapeutic Opportunity for EGFR-Mutant Lung Cancer
description: Our study establishes Trop2 as a therapeutically targetable vulnerability in DTP cells and provides a mechanistic rationale for combining Trop2-ADCs with EGFR-TKIs to prevent resistance and improve outcomes in EGFR-mutant NSCLC. These findings highlight a novel strategy to overcome adaptive resistance and prolong therapeutic efficacy in this patient population.

title: The TNFR2M196R Germline Variant Confers Dual Impact on CAR-T Cell Immunotherapy by Enhancing T-cell Survival and Tumor Proliferation
organization: the First Medical Center, Chinese PLA General Hospital
description: We identify the germline TNFR2M196R SNP (rs1061622) as a pivotal genetic determinant of atypical responses, which was prompted by a patient with low-tumor-burden non-Hodgkin lymphoma who developed severe, persistent cytokine release syndrome (CRS). The TNFR2M196R variant was found to enhance the antitumor efficacy of CAR-T cells by reducing their apoptosis. Paradoxically, however, patients carrying the TNFR2M196R variant exhibited higher rates of early tumor progression. Further investigation revealed that while the TNFR2M196R mutation increased tumor susceptibility to CAR-T-mediated killing, it also accelerated tumor proliferation kinetics. Together, these results establish the TNFR2M196R SNP as a dual-function genetic determinant that modulates both CAR-T cell efficacy and intrinsic tumor behavior, highlighting the critical impact of germline genetics on cancer immunotherapy.

title: Evolution of resistance to KRASG12C inhibitor in a non-small cell lung cancer responder
description: In this study, single-cell sequencing was employed to delineate the dynamic alterations within the CD8+CD161hi T cell population in the peripheral blood of patients harboring the KRASG12C mutation in a detailed manner.

title: Durvalumab plus anlotinib versus durvalumab alone as maintenance treatment in extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer (DURABLE): a multicenter, randomized, phase II trial
description: Tumor tissue samples were collected at baseline. Peripheral blood was collected at four time points: baseline (T0), first assessment (T1), before randomization (T2), and disease progression after randomization (T3). From these blood samples, circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) was isolated and subjected to comprehensive genomic profiling covering 571 cancer-related genes (AmoyDx, China) on the Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform (Illumina, San Diego, CA, USA), as previously described29. Blood tumor mutational burden (bTMB) was calculated based on the number of detected somatic mutations as previously reported30. Meanwhile, RNA sequencing was performed on tumor biopsy using the Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform after RNA extraction and cDNA library preparation (detailedly described in supplementary appendix).

organization: Pu er People's Hospital, Kunming University of Science and Technology Affiliated Hospital
description: This study contains RNA sequencing data generated from the human lung adenocarcinoma cell line PC-9. Transcriptome sequencing was performed in SLC52A3-knockdown cells and control cells, with three biological replicates in each group. The six samples included in this study are PC-9-WT-01, PC-9-WT-02, PC-9-WT-03, PC-9-1761-01, PC-9-1761-02, and PC-9-1761-03. These data were generated to investigate transcriptomic changes associated with SLC52A3 depletion in lung adenocarcinoma cells.

KRAS amplification and TP53 missense mutation were detected by next-generation sequencing (NGS).

description: To understand the spatial organization of cells within the TME of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after neoadjuvant ICB-chemotherapy, we obtained spatial transcriptomics data from six post-treatment NSCLC patients using Stereo-seq.

description: In this study, we utilized bioinformatics analysis, gene-edited mouse models, and multiple biochemical approaches to reveal that ENO1 K420 lactylation promotes its binding to YAP1, thereby stabilizing YAP1 protein and driving LUAD progression and osimertinib resistance.

title: WD-3 Reshaped Gut Microbiota Homeostasis and Serum Metabolites to Promote the Efficacy of immunotherapy for Lung Cancer
organization: Wuxi Hospital Affiliated to Nanjing University of Chinese Medicine
description: Feces and serum of patients with lung cancer responded or non-responded to anti-PD-1 mAb were collected. 16S sequencing of feces and non-targeted metabolomics analysis of serum were carried out to figure out gut microbiota and serum metabolites candidates related to anti-PD-1 treatment effect.

title: CircRNA-Encoded RIPK1-98 Protein Drives Lung Adenocarcinoma Progression
description: Biological unexplored matter remains poorly understood. Using integrated multi-omics approaches, this study identifies and characterizes previously unrecognized proteins encoded by circular RNAs (circRNAs) in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). Notably, a novel protein, RIPK1-98, modulates CDK2-dependent cell cycle regulation to facilitate tumor proliferation. These findings suggest that RIPK1-98 may serve as both a biomarker for cell cycle progression and a potential therapeutic target in LUAD.

title: NSCLC sample mutation dataset containing PD-L1 data
description: This dataset contains gene mutation information from 3185 NSCLC patients, and all samples contain PD-L1 data, TMB, MSI, and corresponding clinical information.

title: Single-cell RNA-seq of non-small cell lung cancer in response to neoadjuvant combinational immunotherapies
description: Multiple combinational immunotherapy regimens are currently being explored in clinical trials. While preclinical studies have provided insights into the mechanisms of these regimens, their efficacy and impact on the tumor microenvironment (TME) in patients are not fully understood. Understanding the dynamics of the TME during different combinational therapies is crucial for optimizing immunotherapy approaches, particularly for patients who do not respond to treatment. Here, we performed single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis on tumor samples from patients diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). These samples include paired pre-treatment biopsy and post-neoadjuvant treatment samples with PD-1 inhibitors in combination with either chemotherapy or anti-VEGFA therapy. By integrating the transcriptomic profiles of more than1 million cells, we identified shared and distinct mechanisms within the TME in response to different therapy regimens.

title: PD-1/ PD-L1 Bispecific Antibody IBI318 Combined with Lenvatinib in Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer with Acquired Resistance to Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors
description: In this study, we initiated a prospective, open-label, single-arm clinical trial (ClinicalTrial.gov: NCT04777084) aimed at evaluating the therapeutic impact and safety profile of the bispecific anti-PD-1/PD-L1 antibody IBI318 in combination with the receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) inhibitor lenvatinib. The trial enrolled patients with advanced or metastatic NSCLC lacking actionable driver mutations and exhibiting acquired resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), we analyzed changes in the tumor microenvironment (TME) before treatment to identify specific cell populations associated with therapeutic response.

title: RNA sequencing following RASA4 knockdown in small cell lung cancer cells
organization: Hefei Institutes of Physical Science, Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Methylome profiling of tumor tissue and plasma cell-free DNA identifies a novel epigenetic silenced tumor suppressor RASA4 in small cell lung cancer
organization: Hefei Institutes of Physical Science, Chinese Academy of Sciences
description: We performed Methylated DNA Immunoprecipitation Sequencing (MeDIP-seq) to conduct whole-genome methylation profiling on paired primary tumor tissues and adjacent normal tissues from patients with limited-stage small cell lung cancer (LS-SCLC) who underwent surgical treatment. In parallel, blood samples collected from patients with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) before chemotherapy and at disease progression after developing chemoresistance were also analyzed.

title: mRNA half-life profiling of METTL3 inhibitor STM2457-treated human large cell lung carcinoma cell line
description: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) methylation has emerged as a prevalent RNA modification that extensively impacts various physiological and pathological processes via various post-transcriptional readout effects in mammals. High-throughput methylome profiling has outlined the landscape of m6A modification sites, but their downstream readouts require comprehensive investigation. METTL3 has been highlighted as the core component of the m6A writer complex, which can be effectively inhibited by the inhibitor STM2457. Therefore, to investigate the readout effect of m6A on the human large cell lung carcinoma cell line H460, cells were grouped into STM2457-treated and control cells. Actinomycin-D (a transcription inhibitor)-treated time-series transcriptome sequencing (with ERCC spike-in) was employed to profile and compare the mRNA half-life levels between the two groups. The results suggested that the half-life of thousands of m6A target genes was perturbed by the METTL3 inhibitor STM2457 in the H460 cell line.

title: A translational study on the survival outcome and molecular mechanism of PD-L1 expression status in EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma treated with osimertinib
description: Highly expressed PD-L1 is associated with poor clinical outcomes in EGFR-mutated NSCLC patients receiving EGFR TKIs. However, the prognostic significance of PD-L1 expression with first-line osimertinib remains unclear. In this retrospective study, we analyzed 317 EGFR-mutated stage III-IV lung adenocarcinoma patients treated with first-line osimertinib. High PD-L1 expression demonstrated significantly shorter progression-free survival (12.2 vs. 21.5 months, p<0.001) and overall survival (31.9 vs. 38.9 months, p=0.025) compared to low PD-L1 expression. Transcriptomic analysis revealed upregulation of IFNG and IL-6/JAK/STAT3 signaling pathways in high PD-L1 tumors.Flow cytometry identified an increased proportion of CD56bright natural killer cells in high PD-L1 patients. In vitro experiments demonstrated that IFNG induces PD-L1 expression via STAT3 activation.

title: Transcriptome Profiling of Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocyte-Mediated Cytotoxicity against Patient-Derived Lung Cancer Organoids
description: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a leading cause of cancer mortality, and therapies utilizing tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) show significant promise. However, molecular signatures defining a productive TIL-mediated response remain poorly characterized. Here, we establish a patient-derived organoid and autologous TIL co-culture platform to show that expanded TILs mediate potent, specific cytotoxicity against NSCLC organoids. This functional response is associated with a crucial shift in T-cell states from proliferative towards effector memory phenotypes and involves activating key signaling networks, including the TNF and IL-17 pathways. Furthermore, T-cell receptor (TCR) analysis confirms the expansion process selectively enriches tumor-associated clonotypes, resulting in a more focused repertoire. This work delineates the transcriptional and clonal signatures of an effective anti-tumor immune response, providing a robust framework to guide next-generation personalized TIL therapies.

description: This trial aimed to evaluate the safety and feasibility of administering sintilimab-based induction therapy for potentially resectable stage III NSCLC to offer a more advantageous therapeutic strategy. Bulk RNA-seq and WES of baseline and post-treatment samples were conducted to investigate the tumor microenvironment and identify potential biomarkers.

title: ATAC-Seq Analysis of Chromatin Accessibility in NCI-H1688 Small Cell Lung Cancer (SCLC) Cells with XPO1 Knockdow
organization: Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital
description: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) remains one of the most aggressive malignancies, with limited advances in targeted therapies and only incremental benefits from immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), largely due to its profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and lack of precision strategies to reprogram it. Here, we identify Exportin 1 (XPO1) as an upstream orchestrator of immune suppression in SCLC. Mechanistically, XPO1 promotes TRIM21-mediated nuclear export and proteasomal degradation of IRF3, repressing the immunostimulatory cytokine TNFSF15. TNFSF15 loss drives differentiation of TREM2+ macrophages and dictates immune exclusion. These macrophages attenuate STAT1 signaling in tumor cells, downregulating MHC I and impairing antigen presentation. Pharmacologic or genetic XPO1 blockade restores TNFSF15, constrains TREM2+ macrophage differentiation and enhances anti-PD-1 efficacy in vivo.

title: Enhancer Reprogramming Reveals the tumorigenic role of PTPRZ1  in Lung Squamous Cell Carcinoma
description: Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) remains a lethal malignancy with limited therapeutic advancements, underscoring the need to identify novel oncogenic drivers. Here, we integrated multi-omics analyses-including ChIP-seq, bulk RNA-seq, single-cell ATAC/RNA-seq, and spatial transcriptomics-to delineate enhancer-driven transcriptional networks in 59 matched LUSC tumors and adjacent normal tissues.

title: CTLA-4 Haploinsufficiency (CHAI syndrome) presenting as Colchicine-Resistant Familial Mediterranean Fever: expanding the differential diagnosis in autoinflammatory syndromes
description: we discuss a 5-year-old boy who presented with recurrent fevers, gastrointestinal symptoms, thrombocytopenia, and features resembling Familial Mediterranean Fever (FMF) that were unresponsive to colchicine treatment. Despite identifying a positive MEFV mutation, colchicine did not alleviate the symptoms. Further genetic analysis revealed a heterozygous mutation in the CTLA4 gene, confirming a diagnosis of CHAI syndrome. The patient demonstrated significant improvement after starting treatment with the IL-1 receptor antagonist.

title: Sintilimab combined with chemotherapy for first line treatment of locally advanced or metastatic pulmonary lymphoepithelioma-like carcinomaRunning head: Sintilimab Combined Chemotherapy for Untreated PLELC
organization: First Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University
description: Pulmonary lymphoepithelioma like carcinoma is a distinct subtype of non-small cell lung cancer associated with Epstein-Barr virus and a unique immune environment. Currently, there is no established standard treatment protocol for PLELC. A multicenter, single arm, phase II study is conducted on 30 patients, who had a histologic diagnosis of locally advanced or metastatic PLELC without any prior systemic treatment. Patients received four cycles of sintilimab plus gemcitabine and carboplatin, followed by sintilimab maintenance. At a median follow up of 42.4 months, the objective response rate was 73.3%, with a disease control rate of 100% . The median progression free survival was 13.5 months, and the median overall survival was 46.9 months. Grade more than 3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 70.0% of patients, with neutropenia being the most common.Sintilimab plus gemcitabine and carboplatin showed promising efficacy with manageable safety as first-line treatment for advanced PLELC.

title: Correlation between lung microbiota and detection of some pathogenicmicroorganism in patients with severe pneumonia in ICU
description: Human intestinal fungi and pulmonary fungi play an important role in human microecology and health. Aggressive fungal infections can occur in people with Covid-19 or severe influenza, especially after treatment with immunosuppressive drugs such as dexamethasone or IL-6 inhibitors. No studies have been conducted to evaluate the effects of early pulmonary and intestinal fungal microecological changes on the risk of secondary fungal infection in patients with viral pneumonia. This study plans to collect alveolar lavage fluid, stool and serum from severe pneumonia patients admitted to ICU from 2023 to 2024, and collect clinical data of patients to identify the pulmonary and intestinal fungal microecological changes and the risk of secondary fungal infection in patients of different groups, so as to find targeted treatment plans.

title: Salvianolic acid F inhibits proliferation, migration and invasion of lung cancer cells via CXCL5
description: Lung cancer represents a malignant neoplasm that has affected human populations for an extended period. Despite the implementation of diverse therapeutic approaches that have notably enhanced patient survival rates, the associated adverse effects remain inadequately addressed. Recent research has identified that traditional Chinese medicine possesses distinctive benefits in the management of tumors. In our study, we isolated and extracted a monomeric compound from Danshen, which demonstrated a significant inhibitory effect on the proliferation of lung cancer cells.

title: Anlotinib Enhances the Efficacy of KRAS-G12C Inhibitors through c-Myc/ORC2 Axis Inhibition in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
organization: Shanghai Chest Hospital of Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine
description: The KRAS-G12C mutation, occurring in approximately 14% of lung adenocarcinomas, has emerged as a critical target for precision medicine strategies. While KRAS-G12C inhibitors, including sotorasib and adagrasib, have shown promise in clinical trials, their efficacy is limited by primary and acquired resistance mechanisms. This study explored the potential of combining anlotinib, a multi-target tyrosine kinase inhibitor, with KRAS-G12C inhibitors to overcome these resistance challenges in NSCLC treatment. Our results demonstrated that anlotinib improved the sensitivity to KRAS-G12C inhibitors in primary and acquired resistance settings, both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, the combination therapy inhibited c-Myc/ORC2 signaling, leading to cell cycle arrest and apoptosis. These findings suggest that the combination of anlotinib and KRAS-G12C inhibitors represents a promising novel therapeutic approach for KRAS-G12C-mutant NSCLC.

title: Identification of altered immune landscape at single-cell resolution and its association with poor immune checkpoint inhibitor responses in NSCLC brain metastasis
description: Brain metastasis, a common complication of advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), leads to poor prognosis and reduces the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). However, the mechanisms underlying this diminished ICI response remain unclear. Therefore, we comprehensively analyzed RNA sequencing data derived from 112,200 immune cells isolated from primary and brain metastatic NSCLC single-cell samples.

description: We generated in-house RNase R-treated RNA-seq data for three lung cell lines (A549, NCI-H23, and HSAEC). Amplicon sequencing of NCI-H23 was performed by Novogene.

title: Immune Correlates of Response and Resistance to Neoadjuvant Chemo-immunotherapy in Non-small Cell Lung Cancer
description: To understand mechanisms of primary resistance, we followed a sufficiently large cohort of NSCLC patients receiving neoadjuvant immunotherapy, and profiled post-treatment samples using single-cell RNA and T cell receptor (TCR) sequencing. By associating tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) with response, we uncovered heterogeneous mechanisms of response and major mechanisms of primary resistance, providing insights into strategic developments of combination regimens.

title: Transcriptome study of the interaction of six A. baumannii phages with A549 lung epithelial cells.
organization: Wuhan Institute of Virology, Chinese Academy of Sciences
description: In this study, we evaluate the influence of six morphologically different Acinetobacter baumannii phages on A549 cells after a 12 hour challenge.

title: Neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 therapy for human non-small cell lung cancer
organization: The second affiliated hospital zhejiang university school of medicine
description: Neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 therapy for human non-small cell lung cancer

title: Single-cell analysis reveals transcriptomic features and therapeutic targets in primary pulmonary lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma.
organization: Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University
description: The snRNA-seq identified a crucial malignant subpopulation of PPLELC with overexpression of AKT3 and FGFR2, related to late clinical state, large tumor size and lymph nodes metastasis. Moreover, higher expression of AKT3 and FGFR2 is associated with worse prognosis in PPLELC patients. Enzastaurin, AKT3 inhibitor, and Erdafitinib, FGFR2 inhibitor have shrunk the PPLELC tumor in PDXs. The different gene modules of T lymphocytes, B lymphocytes and macrophages were identified in their subgroups. The multiple ligand-receptor interactions of intercellular communications were depicted in the PPLELC microenvironment.

title: Drug repurposing to overcome osimertinib resistance in non-small cell lung cancer
organization: The Chinse University of Hong Kong
description: Novel Met-inhibitory drug candidates were identified and repurposed to overcome osimertinib resistance in non-small cell lung cancer. RNA sequencing was conducted to investigate the differentially expressed genes after drug treatment

title: Early-Age Onset Lung Cancer in Young East Asian Populations: Unveiling Genetic and Immune Signatures
description: Focusing on young NSCLC patients, this study examines the mutation types of the HER2 gene and proposes potential biomarkers and treatment strategies.

title: CCN1 is a therapeutic target upregulated in EML4-ALK mutant lung adenocarcinoma reversibly resistant to alectinib
description: There is limited understanding of the phenomenon of reversible resistance, which is characterized by tumor cells becoming resistant to drugs for a period of time and regaining sensitivity when the drugs are withdrawn. In this study, alectinib was used to induce reversible resistance in EML4-ALK positive lung cancer cell lines. Changes in transcriptional expression profiles were examined by RNA sequencing of reversibly resistant cell lines, and significant changes in CCN1 were detected after treatment discontinuation and after repeated dosing with alectinib. Targeting CCN1 inhibits tumor cell proliferation and angiogenesis and restores sensitivity to alectinib. Further studies suggest that CCN1 may affect the expression of VEGFA by affecting AKT phosphorylation, and changes in NF-kB may affect the activation of CCN1-AKT-VEGFA pathway. Inhibition of NF-kB or CCN1 receptors increases alectinib sensitivity, suggesting that NF-kB and CCN1 may play a key role in reversible resistance.

title: Effective production of highly functional macrophages from human pluripotent stem cells for cancer immunotherapy
organization: Shenzhen Campus of Sun Yat-sen University
description: Generation of chimeric antigen receptor macrophages (CAR-M) from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) offers new prospects for tumor immunotherapy, but is currently challenged by low differentiation efficiency and limited function. In this study, we developed a highly efficient monolayer-based system that can produce around 6,000 CAR-M from a single hPSC within 3 weeks. Based on screens of modified structures, we identified macrophage-compatible CAR structures with optimized ability to generate hPSC-CAR-M with stable CAR expression and maintained the pro-inflammatory characteristics of macrophages to enhance their tumoricidal activity in vitro. To overcome the loss of tumoricidal activity of hPSC-CAR-M in vivo, we used interferon-r and a toll-like receptor 4 agonist to activate the innate immune system.

title: Pembrolizumab Combined with Chemotherapy for Resectable Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma (Keystone-001)
organization: Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital
description: Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab pluschemotherapy, followed by Da Vinci robotic-assisted surgery, was effective and safe forresectable ESCC. The expansion of TRGC2+ NKT cells in peripheral blood maypredict treatment response.

title: The effect of intratumoral heterogeneity of genome and immune microenvironment on relapse in patients with localized small cell lung cancer
organization: The Cancer Hospital of the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences (Zhejiang Cancer Hospital)
description: The GeoMx DSP instrument was employed to obtain the transcriptomics and proteomics from tumor, stroma, and para-tumor region from 44 patients diagnosed with SCLC at Zhejiang Cancer Center, Cancer Hospital of The University of Chinese Academy of Science.

title: Inhibiting RNA m6A Causes an Interferon Response in Cancer and Sustain T cell Function to Improve Cancer Immunotherapy
organization: Guangzhou Institutes of Biomedicine and Health, Chinese Academy of Sciences
description: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) is the most abundant mRNA modification catalyzed by METTL3. This study showed METTL3 inhibited activated interferon response genes including Isg15 and Oas2. METTL3 inhibiting augmented sensitivity to ICB therapy with anti-PD-1 in B16 melanoma mouse model and can also sustain T cell function.

title: Sintilimab Combined with Anlotinib and Chemotherapy as Second-Line or Later Therapy in Extensive-Stage Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Phase II Clinical Trial
organization: Shandong Cancer Hospital and Institute, Shandong First Medical University and Shandong Academy of Medical Sciences
description: Phase II trial at Shandong Cancer Hospital tested anlotinib, sintilimab, and chemo in ES-SCLC as 2nd line. 25 patients, 6-cycle combo, mPFS 6.0m, mOS 13.4m, ORR 60%, DCR 76%, 80% TRAEs, 12% Grade 3+. ctDNA: low bTMT linked to better outcomes, KMT2D mutation in resistance. Trial N: ChiCTR2100049390.

title: Efficacy of Cadonilimab and Anlotinib Combination in Treating Multiple Drug-Resistant Pulmonary Large Cell Neuroendocrine Carcinoma: Insights from a Case Report and Literature Review
description: This study assesses the efficacy of different treatment approaches, such as the use of cadonilimab and anlotinib, by monitoring the patient's response through various cycles of treatment. This includes the use of computed tomography scans to evaluate treatment response. We believe that our study makes a significant contribution to the literature because the case report explores alternative treatment options for pulmonary large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma patients who have shown resistance to traditional programmed death 1 monoclonal antibodies and multiple chemotherapies. The use of cadonilimab and anlotinib in this context is highlighted, suggesting that this combination could be a potential treatment strategy.

title: Phase II Trial of Neoadjuvant Camrelizumab and Apatinib in Patients with Resectable Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer: Survival and Dynamic Circulating Tumor DNA Analyses
organization: National Cancer Center/National Clinical Research Center for Cancer/Cancer Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences and Peking Union Medical College
description: Exploratory analysis of ctDNA-based dynamic monitoring of prognostic guidance value of neoadjuvant camrelizumab and apatinib in patients of resectable of non-small cell lung cancer

title: Microenvironment compartmentalization of NSCLC after immunotherapy revealed by single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses
description: PD-(L)1 immune checkpoint inhibitors have shifted the treatment paradigm of advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Here, we combined single cell and spatial transcriptomics to identify the spatial landscape of the NSCLC tumor microenvironment (TME) during immunotherapy. Multidimensional bioinformatics analyses revealed distinct spatial compartmentalization of the TME. Our study provides novel insights into the complex spatiotemporal ecosystem of NSCLC and offers clues for combinational therapies.

title: Neoadjuvant therapy with immune checkpoint blockade and chemotherapy for NSCLC
organization: The Fifth Medical Center of Chinese PLA General Hospital
description: Multi-omics analysis uncovers prognostic biomarkers and tumorecosystem dynamics during sequential neoadjuvant treatment of dose-limiting chemotherapy combined with sintilimab for non-small cell lungcancer.

title: Preclinical study and phase II trial of adapting low-dose radiotherapy to immunotherapy in small cell lung cancer
organization: West China Hospital of Sichuan University
description: Raw data for single-cell RNA sequencing of SCLC patients generated in this study.

title: Tumor microenvironment assessment-based signatures for predicting response to immunotherapy in non-small cell lung cancer
description: Immune checkpoint blockades (ICBs) have significantly altered the treatment paradigm for patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without driver mutations, but not all patients experience durable benefits. Predictive biomarkers are needed to identify patients who may benefit from ICBs. We obtained tumor specimens from NSCLC patients before anti-PD-1 inhibitor treatment and performed transcriptomic analysis to generate tumor microenvironment characteristics. Based on tumor microenvironment data, we sought to establish biomarker to predict immunotherapy efficacy for NSCLC.

title: Cuproptosis improves immunotherapy outcomes by upregulating HLA-DRA expression which promotes the aggregation of CD4+ and CD8+T lymphocytes in clear cell renal cell carcinoma
organization: The First Affiliated Hospital of Harbin Medical University
description: To investigate the possible effects of cuproptosis and HLA-DRA on the tumor immune microenvironment, we obtained plasmid-transfected HLA-DRA-OE-A498 cells after treatment with elesclomol and Cu for 24 h. The cells were washed three times with PBS and then collected and subjected to transcriptome sequencing analysis

title: Mechanisms of resistance to 5-Fluorouracil and reversal strategies in lung cancer and breast cancer treatment.
description: Overcoming 5-Fluorouracil resistance in human cancer cells by the combination of 5-Fu and Wnt inhibitors through the inhibition of Wnt/beta-Catenin signalling pathway.

title: Biological Effects of Electronic Cigarettes on Lung Bronchial Epithelial Cells
description: Multidimensional Assessment of the Biological Effects of Electronic Cigarettes on Lung Bronchial Epithelial Cells

title: Sintilimab in Combination with Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy and Granulocyte-Macrophage Colony-Stimulating Factor in Metastatic Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Multicenter Phase 2 Trial
description: This single-arm, multicenter, phase 2 trial (NCT04106180) investigated the triple combination of Sintilimab, stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) and granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Paired tissue samples from an unirradiated tumor lesion were collected before and after SBRT but before the initiation of the first cycle of Sintilimab and GM-CSF treatment. RNA sequencing was performed using these samples.

title: Excess Fatty acid Shapes Metabolic Codependences in Steatotic NAFLD-HCC to Suppression of Immunotherapy
organization: The First Affiliated Hospital of University of Science and Technology of China
description: We performed RNA-seq using HCC cells treated with PAOA for different periods.

title: Twist1 SUMOylation Drives Chemotherapy Resistance in Human Lung Cancer
organization: Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine
description: Twist1, an evolutionarily conserved basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor, plays a pivotal role in facilitating tumor metastasis and augmenting chemotherapy resistance. Our research has uncovered that Twist1 is subject to SUMOylation, with the modification sites precisely identified at lysine residues K38 and K73. The SUMOylation of Twist1 significantly impacts gene expression, contributing to the enhancement of chemotherapy resistance in tumor cells. Our findings underscore the critical function of Twist1 SUMOylation in oncogenic processes, suggesting potential targets for therapeutic intervention aimed at mitigating resistance to chemotherapy.

title: Phosphorylation of AGO2 by TBK1 promotes the formation of oncogenic miRISC in NSCLC
organization: Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine
description: Non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a highly lethal tumor that often develops resistance to targeted therapy. We show that Tank-binding kinase 1 (TBK1) phosphorylates AGO2 at S417 (pS417-AGO2), which promotes NSCLC progression by increasing the formation of microRNA-induced silencing complex (miRISC). High levels of pS417-AGO2 in clinical NSCLC specimens are positively associated with poor prognosis. Interestingly, the treatment with EGFR inhibitor Gefitinib can significantly induce pS417-AGO2, thereby increasing the formation and activity of oncogenic miRISC, which may contribute to NSCLC resistance to Gefitinib. Based on these, we have developed two therapeutic strategies. One is jointly to antagonize multiple oncogenic miRNAs highly expressed in NSCLC and use TBK1 inhibitor Amlexanox reducing the formation of oncogenic miRISC. Another approach is to combine Gefitinib with Amlexanox to inhibit the progression of Gefitinib-resistant NSCLC.

title: Spatially oraanized tumor-stroma boundary determines the efficacy of immunotherapy in colorectal cancer patients
description: Our work therefore uncovered the black box of how the molecular and cellular spatial structures of tumors determine ICBresponse, raising the possibility of reprogramming tumor-stroma boundary for sensitizing immunotherapies in the majority of CRCs

title: Sintilimab with two cycles of chemotherapy for treatment of naive advanced squamous NSCLC: A phase 2 clinical trial
organization: The Affiliated Cancer Hospital of Zhengzhou University, Henan Cancer Hospital
description: This was single-arm, multicenter phase 2 clinical trial involving advanced squamous non-small cell lung cancer (sq-NSCLC) patients who received 2 cycles of nab-paclitaxel/carboplatin and sintilimab, followed by maintenance therapy with sintilimab. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary endpoints included the objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), time to response (TTR), duration of response (DOR), overall survival (OS) and safety indicators. The exploratory endpoints were to access the relationship between biomarkers in tumor tissue and treatment efficacy, and the association between circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) dynamics and PFS.

title: A Prospective Study of Circulating Tumor DNA Serial Monitoring of Tislelizumab immunotherapy Responses and Relapse as second-line monotherapy in metastatic Esophageal cancer
description: We prospectively enrolled and collected endoscopic biopsy samples from 12 patients with advanced ESCC treated with tislelizumab. Plasma was collected before and after every 2-3 treatment cycle of tislelizumab and when disease progression. Targeted sequencing of 425 genes on plasma cell-free DNA, DNA from leukocytes, and fixed esophageal tumor biopsies were performed. The patients underwent imaging analyses every 6-8 weeks until disease progression. The association between status and changes in circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) following tislelizumab immunotherapy and response, tumor progression, and survival was determined.

title: The gut microbiome is associated with recurrence-free survival in patients with resected Stage IIIB-D or Stage IV melanoma treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors
description: We performed shotgun sequencing in pre-treatment stool samples obtained from 674 melanoma patients enrolled in an international, randomized, double-blind, phase III adjuvant trial assessing clinical outcomes following adjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab versus nivolumab, with recruitment spanning three continents and five geographically diverse regions.

title: a patient-specific Lung cancer assembloid model-V1
description: Here, we develop an innovative patient-specific lung cancer assembloid (LCA) model by using a droplet microfluidic technology based on a microinjection strategy. This method enables precise manipulation of clinical micro-samples and rapid generation of LCAs with good intra-batch consistency in size and cell composition. The LCAs recapitulate the inter- and intra-tumoral heterogeneity, TME cellular diversity, genomic and transcriptomic landscape of their parental tumors. This LCA model could construct and identify the functional heterogeneity of cancer-associated fibroblasts that correlates with tumor responses to drug treatments. More importantly, LCA model presents better consistency in drug response profiling compared to the corresponding cancer organoids and accurately replicates the clinical outcomes of patients, suggesting the potential of the LCA model to predict personalized treatments.

title: Safety and tolerability of low-dose radiation and stereotactic body radiotherapy plus sintilimab for treatment-naive stage IV PD-L1+ non-small-cell lung cancer: a phase 1 trial
organization: West China Hospital of Sichuan University
description: This pilot phase I trial aims to investigate the safety and tolerability of anti-programmed cell death-1 (PD-1) monoclonal antibody Sintilimab (also called IBI308) in combination with concurrent stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) and low dose radiotherapy (LDRT) in treating patients with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

title: Transcriptome analysis of pulmonary fibrosis caused by COVID-19 or systemic lupus erythematosus
description: The COVID-19 pandemic poses a huge threat to public health, and pulmonary fibrosis is one of the symptoms of severe cases of infection. Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a multi-system autoimmune disease with pulmonary fibrosis as one of its symptoms. We conducted a preliminary study on the mechanism of pulmonary fibrosis caused by these two diseases, providing theoretical guidance for clinical treatment. Our group investigated the transcriptional characteristics of the occurrence and progression of pulmonary fibrosis in these two diseases, and conducted pathological and transcriptome analysis of lung graft specimens for COVID-19 and SLE fibrosis.

title: Low-dose radiotherapy recruits TCF1+PD-1+CD8+ T cells to enhance efficacy of immunotherapy in small cell lung cancer
organization: West China Hospital of Sichuan University
description: Raw data for single-cell RNA sequencing of SCLC patients generated in this study.

title: HLA-I evolutionary divergence confers response to PD-1 blockade plus chemotherapy in untreated advanced non-small-cell lung cancer
description: PD-1 blockade plus chemotherapy has become the new standard of care in patients with untreated advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), whereas predictive biomarkers remain unknown. Here, we integrated clinical and HLA class I (HLA-I) genotype data of 427 NSCLC patients treated with first-line PD-1 blockade plus chemotherapy or chemotherapy from two previously reported phase 3 trials and investigated the predictive value of HLA-I evolutionary divergence (HED). HED could predict improved response rates and survival outcomes in patients treated with PD-1 blockade plus chemotherapy but not chemotherapy in both two trials, and its predictive value held in multivariate analysis when adjusted for PD-L1 expression and tumor mutation burden.

title: Blood-based Genomic and Cellular Determinants of Response to Neoadjuvant PD-1 Blockade in Patients with Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer
description: The integrated analyses employed in the current study identified blood-based molecular and cellular signatures that are associated with the responsiveness and overall survival of PD-1/PD-L1 blockade therapy plus chemotherapy.

title: identification of key prognostic genes in lung cancer
description: identification of key prognostic genes in lung cancer, then over-express such genes in tumor cell lines, then co-cultured with fibroblast cell lines, and then sequenced cell lines

title: Single-cell RNA-seq and bulk RNA data of non-small cell lung cancer during neoadjuvant immunotherapy
description: Most patients are still refractory to immunotherapy or acquire resistance. We characterized the single-cell transcriptomes of ~92000 cells from 15 non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) before and after neoadjuvant PD-1 blockade combined with chemotherapy to decode immunotherapy resistance mechanisms. In addition, we also performed bulk RNA-seq from another 24 patients before therapy as a validation cohort. Our study offers invaluable resources for uncovering immunotherapy resistance.

This method enables precise manipulation of clinical micro-samples and rapid generation of LCAs with good intra-batch consistency in size and cell composition. The LCAs recapitulate the inter- and intra-tumoral heterogeneity, TME cellular diversity, genomic and transcriptomic landscape of their parental tumors. This LCA model could construct and identify the functional heterogeneity of cancer-associated fibroblasts that correlates with tumor responses to drug treatments. More importantly, LCA model presents better consistency in drug response profiling compared to the corresponding cancer organoids and accurately replicates the clinical outcomes of patients, suggesting the potential of the LCA model to predict personalized treatments.

title: Viral reactivation in the lungs of patient with severe pneumonia is associated with lung microbiota
organization: First Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University School of Medicine
description: Purpose: Virus reactivation in the lungs of patients with severe pneumonia is associated with increased mortality. To date, rare studies have reported the correlation between viral reactivation in the lungs and lung microbiota. Methods: The bronchoalveolar lavage fluid of 49 patients with severe pneumonia admitted to the Department of Critical Care Medicine of the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University School of Medicine was collected. Virus reactivation was detected by Metagenomic next-generation sequencing and lung microbiota was detected by 16S rRNA.

title: Transcriptome-wide m6A Methylation Profiling of human lung cancer tissue by m6A-seq
organization: Frontiers Science Center for Disease-related Molecular Networks, West China Hospital, Sichuan University, Chengdu, Sichuan, China
description: By performing m6A-seq analysis on lung tissue from LUAD patients, we want to identify the m6A methylation pattern on primary tumor tissue and paired non-cancerous adjacent tissues.

title: Precision medicine of lung cancer using molecular probes in clinical translational study
organization: Frontiers Science Center for Disease-related Molecular Networks, West China Hospital, Sichuan University, Chengdu, Sichuan, China
description: our major aim of the study is to identify the subset of patients who may benefit from EGFR-TKIs therapy, and hence to design appropriate treatment strategies for optimized clinical outcome. Specifically, the biopsied samples of lung cancer patients are subjected to quantitative detection of EGFR mutations (L858R, 19del) using the fluorescent probe HX103 and FACS analysis. Combined with the results from gene sequencing and HX103 labeling, it will allow us to rapid and accurate determine EGFR mutations in lung cancer patients.

title: Role of induction immune-checkpoint inhibitors for resectable oncogene-mutant non-small cell lung cancer: A multicenter pooled analysis
description: Despite limited efficacy of immunotherapy for advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with driver mutations, question as to whether neoadjuvant immunotherapy could be clinically valuable in those patients warrants further investigation. We utilized 34 oncogene-mutant NSCLC treated with induction immunotherapy from a large consecutive multicenter cohort along with multi-omics analysis on sequential paired samples. The overall response rate was 61.8% while 2 patients had disease progression. The major pathological response (MPR) rate was 41.2% (14/34) and pathological complete response (pCR) rate was 14.7% (5/34). Specifically, induction immunotherapy plus chemotherapy yielded the most superior efficacy among erlotinib and chemotherapy for resectable EGFR-mutant NSCLC. Our results firstly indicated clinical feasibility of induction immunotherapy for resectable oncogene-mutant NSCLC.

title: Clinical genomic factors associated with immunotherapy efficacy in real-world patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer
organization: Shandong Cancer Hospital and Institute, Shandong First Medical University and Shandong Academy of Medical Sciences
description: The purpose of this study was to retrospectively analyze the clinical and genomic characteristics of 59 patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors at our center, and to explore the relevant clinical characteristics and biomarkers affecting the efficacy.

title: 3D genomics of Lung cancer
description: Characterize three-dimentional chromatin organization of lung cancer cellline

title: Genomic and proteomic detection and correlation analysis of neoantigens in non-small cell lung cancer
organization: Peking Union Medical College Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College
description: In recent years, Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have become an important strategy for the treatment of patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). As an important biomarker and potential immunotherapeutic target, neoantigen plays an important role in the treatment and prognosis of NSCLC patients. Whole exome sequencing (WES) was performed on histological samples of enrolled patients, and neoantigen was predicted by Neopipe. The relationship between candidate neoantigen and clinicopathological characteristics was analyzed. The relationship between prediction of neoantigen and gene mutation features was analyzed.

title: Predicting durable responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors in non-small-cell lung cancer using a multi-feature model
description: Predicting durable responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors in non-small-cell lung cancer using a multi-feature model

title: The web-based multiplex PCR primer design software Ultiplex and the associated experimental workflow: Up to 100- plex multiplicity
description: Ultiplex was developed as a free online multiplex primer design tool with a user-friendly web-based interface (http://ultiplex.igenebook.cn). To evaluate the performance of Ultiplex, 294 out of 295 (99.7%) target primers were successfully designed. A total of 275 targets produced qualified primers after primer filtration, and 271 of those targets were successfully clustered into one compatible PCR group and could be covered by 108 primers. The designed primer group stably detected the rs28934573(C>T) mutation at lower than a 0.25% mutation rate in a series of samples with different ratios of HCT-15 and HaCaT cell line DNA.

title: Tumor Microenviroment Characteristics in a Patient with HER2 Mutant Lung Squamous Cell Carcinoma harboring High PD-L1 Expression Who Presented Hyperprogressive Disease
organization: Second Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University School of Medicine
description: High PD-L1 expression in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is evident to predict elevated immunotherapy efficacy, to which NSCLC with onco-driver genes mutations is probed with poor responsiveness. Thus, it is of great interest to investigate how effective immune monotherapy is in the presence of concurrent high PD-L1 expression and driving genes mutation.

title: Long Non-coding RNA NR2F1-AS1 Induces Breast Cancer Lung Metastatic Dormancy by Regulating NR2F1 and deltaNp63
organization: Shanghai Institute of Nutrition and Health, Chinese Academy of Sciences
description: Disseminated tumor cells often fall into a long term of dormant stage, characterized by decreased proliferation but sustained survival, in distant organs before awakening for metastatic growth. However, the regulatory mechanism of metastatic dormancy and awakening is largely unknown. Here, we show that the epithelial-like and mesenchymal-like subpopulations of breast cancer stem-like cells (BCSCs) demonstrate different levels of dormancy and tumorigenicity in lungs. LncRNA NR2F1-AS1 (NAS1) is highly expressed in mesenchymal-like breast cancer stem-like cells and promotes cancer cell dissemination and lung metastatic dormancy by regulating BCSC heterogeneity through NR2F1-deltaNp63 axis.

title: Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of small cell lung cancer reveals its immunosuppressive microenvironment and implies the benefit of immunotherapy
description: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a deadly neuroendocrine malignancy without efficient treatment. Due to the scarcity of fresh tumor samples, the heterogeneity and cellular diversity of SCLC at the single-cell level remain to be elucidated. We utilized the endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration (EBUS-TBNA) sampling strategy to examine the single-cell transcriptome of metastatic lymph node samples from 7 SCLC patients.

title: Establishment of lung tumor organoids
description: We established organoids from patient derived lung tumor tissues and compared the genetic alterations in the tumor organoids and the original tumor tissues. We demonstrated that tumor organoids retained the genetic profiles of the parental tissues.

title: ctDNA concentration, MIKI67mutations and hyper-progressive disease related gene mutations are prognostic markers for Camrelizumab and Apatinib combined multiline treatment in advanced NSCLC
description: Immunotherapy by immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) has showed outstanding efficacy in the treatment of advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The combination of immunotherapy with anti-angiogenic therapy exhibited enhanced efficacy in multiline treatment. However, the potential biomarkers for predicting and monitoring the therapeutic response of the combined therapy remain undefined. In this study, we performed a pilot study by prospectively recruiting 22 advanced NSCLC patients who failed to previous lines of chemotherapy, chemoradiotherapy, TKI therapy, surgery, or any combination of the therapies, and investigated the prognostic factors for patients who received anti-PD-1 (Camrelizumab) and anti-angiogenic (Apatinib) combined therapy.
